leading_positions.synthesis: Four members put optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) first in their round-1 configurations. They share the same two laureates, emphasis on independent reproduction at the 1e-18 level across laboratories, and a preference for a citation built on the magic-wavelength lattice concept rather than on the redefinition of the second. They differ in emphasis: Kroll stresses the many-body and applications record, Lindroth the secure theory-experiment agreement, Johansson reached this position only after moving from circuit QED, and the chair moved from IceCube. Not shared: all four concede the overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and the uncredited Lemonde, Gill, Hollberg and Ludlow contributions, and they do not agree on how far these weaken the case. Eriksson and Mehlig rank it eighth and seventh respectively, and Mehlig and Danielsson question its discovery content or timing.

Three members put magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) first, with a theory-plus-experiment trio and a citation framed around flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity rather than a settled pairing mechanism. Their arguments differ in emphasis: Mehlig stresses the simplicity of the mechanism, Olsson the opening of a tunable experimental platform, Eriksson the closing of a prediction-experiment loop. Not shared: the three agree that the field is about eight years old and that the pairing mechanism is open, but they do not agree on whether this is disqualifying, and each names Yuan Cao, the Dean group or earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto work as an attribution exposure. Four other members list B015 as an alternative or fallback, while Danielsson ranks it fifth for timing.

One member prefers topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (2D quantum spin Hall prediction and HgTe observation). Three others (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson) list B053 as an alternative, but no two members who rank it propose the same laureate trio: Eriksson and Olsson would use Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, which omits Mele, while Danielsson and Mehlig argue that splitting Kane and Mele misstates the history. Whether the 3D branch (Hasan) or the 2D chain (Molenkamp, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang outside any trio) should be credited is unresolved.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 configurations are single-part prizes, and no member's preferred configuration combines two ballots.

B057, B015 and B053 are the three candidates that every explicit first choice falls on; B035 appears as an alternative for Kroll and Lindroth, B054 for Danielsson and Pearce, and B021 for Johansson, but none is any member's first choice.

Members across subfields accept that B057 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist (the identical pair Katori and Ye in every opening proposal), and none says it is not prize-worthy; the disagreement concerns ranking and novelty.

Members who prefer B015 and members who prefer B057 both say the citation should avoid claiming a settled superconducting mechanism (B015) or an unfinished redefinition of the second (B057) as part of the discovery.
Several members state that the pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is unresolved while the existence of the correlated phases is reproduced by many groups.
Multiple members treat independent reproduction and control of systematics as the decisive maturity test, and several defer explicitly to colleagues for subfields outside their own.
scientific_disputes: Whether lattice clocks are a distinct discovery (magic-wavelength lattice and quantum-limited many-atom interrogation) or a refinement of the optical-metrology line already recognised in 2005 and 2012; Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce argue the former, Mehlig and Danielsson lean toward the latter.

Whether a platform that opens a new field (B015) outweighs a decisive, quantified measurement advance (B057) as the standard for a prize; Kroll and Mehlig argue this directly, and Olsson raises the original-experiment test.

Whether topological insulators are sufficiently distinct from the topological phase transitions honoured in 2016, and whether the 2D quantum spin Hall chain or the 3D ARPES identification is the decisive experimental step.

Whether circuit QED (B021) is a new fundamental regime or technology-enabling architecture, given the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits; Johansson, who is closest to the field, ranks it first only in his opening and now lists it as an alternative.
Whether IceCube (B054) evidence is mature: the diffuse flux is secure, but individual source identifications rest at about 3 to 4 sigma, and no member now prefers B054 as a first choice.
attribution_disputes: B057: Katori and Ye are the pair in every proposal, but several members flag Lemonde, Gill, Hollberg, Ludlow, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups as potentially decisive for particular milestones; Pearce and Kroll consider them follow-on, while Lindroth and Johansson treat the credit boundary as a live risk.

B015: priority of the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction over earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto work is raised by Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson; Yuan Cao and the Dean group lie outside the credited names.

B053: Danielsson and Mehlig would credit Kane, Mele and Molenkamp; Eriksson and Olsson would credit Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan; Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu fall outside either version. The members disagree on whether omitting Mele or omitting Hasan is the less defensible cut.

B035 and B021: Kroll and Lindroth disagree on the allocation among Borde, Pritchard, Kasevich, Muller and Chu in atom interferometry, and Johansson, Mehlig and Kroll note that Girvin and Devoret are outside the circuit QED trio.
B054: allocation among Halzen, Karle and Spiering with the AMANDA and Baikal lineage is described as not unique.
maturity_disputes: B015 is about eight years old with an unresolved pairing mechanism; Eriksson and Olsson judge reproduction by many groups to be sufficient, while Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll and Danielsson treat the age as a discount.

B057 has more than a decade of cross-laboratory comparison at 1e-18, but the pending redefinition of the second splits the committee into a wait view (Mehlig) and a do-not-wait view (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce).
B053 is described by several members as mature or overdue, but the disagreement over laureates is a reason some members do not rank it first.
B054 source physics is still maturing, and KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD confirmation is at an early stage.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, works in superconducting circuits and states he should recuse himself from deciding B021; Kroll also discloses membership of the WACQT executive team, which bears on B021 and not on B057.
Olsson works in electron microscopy and says she would recuse herself from deciding B048; B048 is not in any member's preferred configuration.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, where Jun Ye is a JILA scientist, and works on ultrastable lasers relevant to clocks; he reports no joint work with Katori or Ye, but this touches the B057 pair he prefers.
Johansson and Olsson share a Chalmers or Gothenburg environment, which Mehlig and Olsson note as institutional proximity, not a scientific link to a shortlisted discovery.
Pearce (chair) works in astroparticle physics adjacent to B054 and discloses no tie to IceCube, so no recusal is flagged; his current preferred ballot is B057.
questions_for_round2: Should the committee treat B057, B015 or B053 as the lead configuration, and what decision rule applies when members split between breadth of agreement (B057, eight rankings) and field-opening novelty (B015)?

For B057, is a citation limited to the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at 1e-18 sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes, and do Lemonde, Gill, Hollberg and Ludlow change the credit?
For B057, does the unfinished redefinition of the second count for or against awarding now, and can members agree that it is a consequence and not a condition of the discovery?

For B015, is eight years of reproduction by many groups sufficient maturity given the unresolved pairing mechanism, and does Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto priority or the omission of Yuan Cao and the Dean group change the three names?
For B053, if the committee goes this way, which three laureates (Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, or Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan) can be defended, and how should Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu be weighed?

Should any member who prefers a single-part prize consider a two-part configuration, for example pairing B057 with B015 or B053 within the three-person-per-prize limit, and what would be dropped from each?

Does the 2025 circuit prize and the disclosed WACQT connections of Johansson and Kroll change whether B021 should be considered at all, and should B054 stay on the table given that no member now places it first?
summary.chair_observation: Round-1 configurations split four to three to one: B057 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce), B015 (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson) and B053 (Danielsson). Several members state positions that were formed before others updated their rankings, so round 2 should confirm current preferences. The disagreement lies mainly in how to weigh a clean, reproduced measurement advance against a newer field-opening platform, and in unsettled attribution for B015 and B053, and not in doubts about the underlying science of any of the three.
